annotations.keyFindings: Alert-level randomisation: median time to a validation decision 42 minutes with a structured protocol against 96 minutes with usual review; missed events too few to compare.
annotations.limitations: One unit, 20 weeks, contamination reported after the first month.

annotations.keyFindings: Four percent of alerts matched a confirmed outbreak within 14 days; artefacts and duplicates caused most false alerts; alerts in older adults had the highest predictive value.
annotations.limitations: One system; outbreak reports may miss small clusters.

annotations.keyFindings: Seventy-one percent of 62 agencies had no written validation procedure; median 45 minutes per alert; dismissed true events rarely measured.
Outcome-blinded panels agreed only moderately (kappa 0.52), and panels aware of outcomes reclassified 18 percent of alerts towards the known outcome.
annotations.limitations: Three-person panels; one set of alerts.

annotations.keyFindings: Staff reported faster validation and easier handovers with a triage checklist; no figures, definitions or comparison period.
annotations.notes: Not rated: no figures, no comparison and no date, so relevance to the local question and method quality cannot be judged.

annotations.keyFindings: Randomising duty days rather than alerts reduced contamination; with about five alerts a day and intracluster correlation near 0.1 the design effect was about 1.4.
Workshop participants listed checklist items and disagreed about escalating small-count rural signals.
annotations.notes: Not rated: a record of opinions with no data and no date.

annotations.keyFindings: In 5 of 11 care home norovirus clusters, action followed the first alert by two days or more, usually after dismissal as an artefact.
annotations.limitations: Case series; homes differed in size and staffing.

claims.text: In a randomised comparison, a structured validation protocol shortened the median time to a validation decision from 96 to 42 minutes.
claims.passage: Randomising alerts to a structured protocol shortened the median time to a validation decision from 96 to 42 minutes.
claims.interpretation: A randomised comparison of procedures is feasible and time to decision is a responsive outcome.

claims.text: Panel review is a weak reference standard: outcome-blinded panels agreed only moderately and outcome-aware panels shifted towards the known outcome.
claims.passage: The authors conclude that panel review is a weak reference standard for estimating the accuracy of validation procedures
claims.interpretation: An accuracy study against panel review would give biased sensitivity and specificity.

claims.text: Randomising duty days rather than alerts reduces contamination at a design effect of about 1.4 with five alerts a day.
claims.passage: With about five alerts a day and an intracluster correlation near 0.1, the design effect was about 1.4.
claims.interpretation: Planning value for a day-randomised design.

claims.text: Only four percent of alerts corresponded to a confirmed outbreak within 14 days.
claims.passage: Four percent of alerts corresponded to a confirmed outbreak or cluster within 14 days.
claims.interpretation: True events will be too few to compare missed events statistically in six months.

claims.text: In 5 of 11 care home norovirus clusters, action followed the first alert by two days or more.
claims.passage: In 5 of the 11 clusters, public health action followed the first alert by two days or more
claims.interpretation: Dismissed true events are the harm to watch.

synthesis: Eight retrieved records; six appraised at abstract level and two undated grey records left unrated. A randomised comparison showed a structured protocol halving time to a validation decision, with contamination between arms; a simulation study shows that randomising duty days limits contamination at a small design effect. Panel review is a weak reference standard because panels disagree and hindsight shifts their judgement, which undermines an accuracy study. Only about four percent of alerts are real, so missed events will be few, and care home clusters show the cost of dismissal. The two undated records report opinions and unquantified claims.
gradeRationale: One randomised comparison and consistent methods evidence support the time outcome and the design choice; missed events rest on case series. Moderate certainty that structured validation can shorten decisions; low certainty about missed events.
summary: Eight retrieved records; six appraised, two undated records not rated; five claims recorded; overall certainty moderate.
